title: Early pregnancy loss, recurrent miscarriage, medical and surgical abortion and MTP Act regulations
subject: ss-obg
refs: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 200: Early Pregnancy Loss
The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 (India)

steps.say: Threatened abortion is characterized by vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy with a closed internal cervical os and documented intrauterine fetal cardiac activity. Expectant management and pelvic rest are advised, as approximately two-thirds of affected pregnancies successfully continue to term.
steps.tx: First-trimester early pregnancy failure is predominantly genetic in origin, with **chromosomal abnormalities** accounting for over 50 percent of all spontaneous miscarriages. Numerical **autosomal trisomies** constitute the single largest category, with **trisomy 16** being the most frequent lethal numerical aneuploidy encountered on cytogenetic analysis of early abortuses.

steps.say: Inevitable abortion occurs when vaginal bleeding is accompanied by cervical dilatation, progressive effacement, or spontaneous rupture of membranes. Because pregnancy expulsion cannot be prevented, clinical management focuses on prompt uterine evacuation to prevent hemorrhage and sepsis.
steps.tx: **Inevitable abortion** is marked by vaginal bleeding with an open internal cervical os and ruptured membranes or cervical effacement, where progression to **pregnancy expulsion** is unavoidable. Immediate clinical intervention prevents severe maternal hemorrhage, painful uterine contractions, and ascending intrauterine infection.

left.title: Threatened Abortion
points: Internal cervical os remains strictly closed
Ultrasound documents viable embryo; 67% reach live birth

right.title: Inevitable Abortion
points: Heavier vaginal bleeding with painful uterine cramps
Internal cervical os is dilated with effacement
Membranes ruptured or bulging; miscarriage cannot be halted

steps.say: Medical management of early abortion combines an antiprogestogen with a synthetic prostaglandin analog. Oral mifepristone at 200 milligrams is administered first, followed 24 to 48 hours later by misoprostol at 800 micrograms administered buccally, sublingually, or vaginally up to 63 days gestation.
steps.tx: First-trimester **medical abortion** up to 63 days (9 weeks) gestation uses **mifepristone** 200 mg orally followed 24 to 48 hours later by **misoprostol** 800 micrograms buccally, sublingually, or vaginally, achieving complete uterine evacuation rates exceeding 95 percent without surgical instrumentation.

nodes.label: Confirm intrauterine pregnancy <= 63 days on ultrasound
Administer oral mifepristone 200 mg (blocks progesterone receptors)
Administer misoprostol 800 micrograms buccally 24 to 48 hours later
Confirm complete expulsion and resolution on follow-up

steps.say: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Amendment Act 2021, legal pregnancy termination up to 20 weeks requires the opinion of one registered medical practitioner. For specified vulnerable categories between 20 and 24 weeks, the statute requires the concurring opinion of two registered medical practitioners.
steps.tx: Under the **MTP Act 2021**, termination up to 20 weeks requires the opinion of **one registered medical practitioner**. Between 20 and 24 weeks gestation, legal termination requires the opinion of **two registered medical practitioners** for specified vulnerable categories, including survivors of sexual assault and minors.

rows: Risk to maternal life/health, contraceptive failure (all women)
Vulnerable categories (rape survivors, minors, physical disability)
Substantial fetal abnormalities diagnosed by specialist panel
Immediately necessary to save the pregnant woman's life

steps.say: Termination of pregnancy beyond 24 weeks is legally permissible under the MTP Act 2021 only for severe fetal anomalies. A state-level four-member Medical Board comprising a gynecologist, pediatrician, radiologist, and government official must officially diagnose and authorize the termination for substantial fetal abnormalities.
steps.tx: Termination beyond 24 weeks under the **MTP Act 2021** is permissible only upon diagnosis of **substantial fetal abnormalities** confirmed by a state-level four-member statutory **Medical Board** comprising a gynaecologist, paediatrician, radiologist or sonologist, and other government-notified specialist members following comprehensive diagnostic imaging.

nodes.label: Identify severe structural or chromosomal fetal anomaly > 24 weeks
Refer patient to state-level statutory Medical Board
Multidisciplinary evaluation: gynaecologist, paediatrician, and radiologist
Medical Board issues formal opinion allowing legal termination beyond 24 weeks

steps.say: Recurrent pregnancy loss warrants a thorough clinical workup to detect parental and anatomical abnormalities. Defined as two or more failed clinical pregnancies, evaluation mandates parental peripheral blood karyotyping, 3D ultrasound or hysteroscopy for uterine anomalies, and screening for antiphospholipid antibodies.
steps.tx: **Recurrent pregnancy loss** is defined as 2 or more failed clinical pregnancies. Recommended evaluation includes **parental karyotyping** for balanced reciprocal or Robertsonian translocations, uterine cavity assessment for septa or synechiae, and screening for **antiphospholipid antibodies** using lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin assays.

rows: Genetic counseling and PGT-SR with IVF

steps.say: Cervical insufficiency presents with silent, painless second-trimester cervical dilation and prolapse of fetal membranes in the absence of uterine contractions. Elective cervical cerclage, using McDonald or Shirodkar techniques, is placed at 12 to 14 weeks in women with classic prior history.
steps.tx: **Cervical insufficiency** classically manifests as silent, painless second-trimester **cervical dilatation** and membrane prolapse without contractions. Patients with typical recurrent mid-trimester pregnancy losses are managed by elective **cervical cerclage** (McDonald or Shirodkar purse-string suture) placed prophylactically at 12 to 14 weeks gestation.

left.title: McDonald Cerclage Technique
points: Simple purse-string suture placed around cervicovaginal junction
No bladder mobilization required; easier to insert and remove
Non-absorbable polyester tape placed at 12 to 14 weeks

right.title: Shirodkar Cerclage Technique
points: Submucosal tape requiring bladder reflection anteriorly
Placed closer to the internal cervical os
May be left in situ for elective cesarean delivery

steps.say: Surgical evacuation of incomplete or septic abortion employs manual vacuum aspiration or electric suction curettage. Prophylactic antibiotic coverage with doxycycline or broad-spectrum parenteral agents is administered to prevent pelvic inflammatory disease and uterine perforation.
steps.tx: **Surgical evacuation** of incomplete or septic miscarriage utilizes **manual vacuum aspiration** or suction curettage under controlled negative suction pressure. Pre-procedure antimicrobial prophylaxis with oral **doxycycline** or broad-spectrum parenteral antibiotics significantly lowers the risk of post-abortal endometritis, pelvic infection, and uterine synechiae formation.
